data.body:
Root causes, 2026-11-12 PST, each reproduced deterministically.
1. test_bridge_sync_honours_an_active_pause: the ref lock's local git bound (_ref_lock._LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS = 5.0 s, a fail-closed production policy) turns a starved host into a correct "treat as HELD" verdict. Reproduced by injecting a timeout into any `git rev-parse --verify` bounded under 6 s: same error text as the sighting. Fix (commit in this ticket's change): the module's stub_pass fixture raises the bound to 60 s for these semantics tests only, following bug ddc8's precedent in tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock.py; the production bound is untouched. All 5 module tests pass with the injected slow git.
2. test_cli_passed_but_unsigned_is_exit_11_with_byte_identical_stderr: the failure itself was "--- Logging error --- ... ValueError: I/O operation on closed file", the stale stderr handler fixed by bald-diagnostic-cricket (a9300a8b2f2). The `Errno 48 ... address already in use` line was misattributed: in the original log (salvaged fix-haddock make-verify.log, port 55506) it is the PytestUnhandledThreadExceptionWarning from tests/unit/test_audit_serve.py::test_await_listening_reports_a_server_that_cannot_bind, which binds a held port deliberately and passed. On current main the facade test passes 3 of 3 with a stderr handler installed under a since-closed stream plus a warning emitted during the test (the exact failing condition). No port is bound by the facade test; nothing to fix there.
